title: Gratin Savoyard
subtitle: A Savoie potato gratin with stock and Gruyere
excerpt: Thinly sliced potatoes cooked slowly in beef stock with melted Gruyere on top. Richer and more golden than a cream gratin. A classic from the French Alps.
sourceNotes: Traditional Savoie recipe using beef stock instead of cream, baked with Gruyere. A regional Alpine dish distinct from gratin dauphinois.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the gratin up to a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the bake time.

content.text: Gratin Savoyard uses beef stock where Dauphinois uses cream. The stock absorbs into the potato layers and leaves a deeper, more savoury result. Use a starchy potato and keep the slices thin so they cook through before the cheese burns.
Heat the oven to 190C. Rub the inside of the gratin dish with the cut garlic, then rub with half the butter.
Layer a third of the potato slices in the dish. Season with salt and pepper. Scatter a third of the cheese and a few thyme leaves on top.
Repeat with two more layers of potato, seasoning, and cheese. Finish with cheese on top.
Pour the hot beef stock over the layers. The stock should come up to just below the top layer.
Dot the remaining butter over the surface. Lay the thyme sprigs on top.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes until deep gold on top and the potatoes are tender when pierced.
Leave to rest for 10 minutes before serving. The stock will be almost fully absorbed.

items.cause: The oven runs hot or the cheese layer is too thick.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil after 40 minutes and remove for the last 10 minutes to re-crisp.

items.symptom: The potatoes are still firm after the full bake time.
items.cause: The slices were cut too thick or packed too tightly.
items.fix: Keep baking in 10-minute intervals. Thin, even slices cook through reliably.

items.cause: The stock was too much for the dish size.
items.fix: Pour off excess liquid before serving, or return to the oven uncovered for 10 minutes.
